```NOTE`
Root cause hypothesis: On button_press within the slider Axes, `_update` sets `self.drag_active=True` and calls `event.canvas.grab_mouse(self.ax)` (sets canvas.mouse_grabber=ax). Mouse grab is only released in `_update` on button_release or press-outside. When the on_changed callback runs clf()+addElements(), the old slider is dropped (global rebound to new slider) and gets garbage-collected → its bound-method callbacks are weakly held and get disconnected → the button_release `_update` never runs → canvas.mouse_grabber stays pointing at the destroyed Axes, blocking all later widget input. Button path differs because Button's callback runs on release, after which no grab is held.

Confirmed code facts:
- SliderBase.__init__ (256-301): drag_active=False; connects button_press/release (+motion if dragging) to self._update; _observers CallbackRegistry(["changed"]).
- Slider._update (529-552): press-in-ax → drag_active=True + grab_mouse; release/out → drag_active=False + release_mouse.
- backend_bases.grab_mouse (2041): raises RuntimeError if mouse_grabber not in (None, ax); else mouse_grabber=ax. release_mouse (2052): clears iff mouse_grabber is ax.
- AxesWidget (110-150): stores ax, canvas, _cids; connect/disconnect_events; no 'active' attr in this rev.

Likely fix: in `_update`, ignore/handle when the widget's Axes is no longer attached to the figure, and ensure grab is released in that case.
